access_type_at_launch: Invite-only Early Access riders via Robotaxi app; in-car safety monitor in front passenger seat (not a driver); ~10-20 Model Y vehicles; flat $4.20 promotional fare
current_status: Active; expanding geofence; mixed supervised/unsupervised fleet
notes: Musk said launch would start with ~10 vehicles (CNBC 2025-06-20/22). Fleet grew and safety monitors began moving from front passenger seat to trailing chase car and then some vehicles went fully unsupervised starting ~2025-12 to 2026-01 (Electrek/CNBC 2026-01-22). Musk's stated goal of 500 vehicles by end of 2025 was not met (Electrek 2025-11-26, "slashes fleet goal from 500 to ~60"). Independent trackers put active unsupervised Austin fleet at roughly 14-42 vehicles at various points Feb-Jun 2026 (see fleet_tracker_scrape.csv). Geofence expanded 5+ times, most recently 2026-06-03 to cover full Austin metro (~245 sq mi) including Pflugerville, Manor, Gigafactory Texas and the airport (CleanTechnica 2026-06-03). NHTSA opened an informal inquiry within a day of launch after erratic-driving videos surfaced (CNBC 2025-06-23); CBS News reported 14 crashes since launch as of its report.

access_type_at_launch: Invite-only for select Tesla owners via Robotaxi app; human safety driver in driver's seat (required under CA DMV testing permit, not a driverless deployment)
current_status: Active but small-scale; safety driver still legally required as of 2026-07; described by CA regulators as a chartered/limousine-style service rather than an autonomous robotaxi deployment
notes: Tesla only holds a CPUC transportation charter-party carrier (TCP) permit plus a CA DMV permit to test with a safety driver; CPUC has confirmed Tesla has NOT applied for the driverless/autonomous passenger service authorization needed to run an actual robotaxi in CA (CNBC 2025-07-25; ABC7 2025-07/2025). Geofence spans from north of the Golden Gate Bridge to San Jose (NotATeslaApp 2025-07-25/2962). Musk stated at the Q4 2025 earnings call (2026-01-28) that the combined Austin+Bay Area fleet was "well over 500" vehicles, but this is not broken out by geography. Independent tracker (Robotaxi Tracker, via Electrek) put active Bay Area fleet at ~107-168 vehicles in April 2026, collapsing to ~9 active by late May 2026 (Electrek 2026-05-26).

access_type_at_launch: Public Robotaxi app (same app as Austin); fully unsupervised (no human safety driver or monitor) from launch, but very small initial fleet (~1-2 vehicles visible at launch per early tracker reports)
official_fleet_size: unknown (city-specific figure never disclosed by Tesla)
notes: Announced as part of a 7-city 1H-2026 expansion list (Dallas, Houston, Phoenix, Miami, Orlando, Tampa, Las Vegas) in Tesla's Q4 2025 shareholder deck released with Q4 2025 earnings on 2026-01-28 (Teslarati). Launched with Houston on 2026-04-18, four days ahead of Tesla's Q1 2026 earnings report (mlq.ai; NotATeslaApp #4004; Electrek 2026-04-18). Initial geofence ~30-35 sq mi. Texas DMV (SB 2807) registration data (a state regulatory record, not a Tesla-disclosed per-city number) showed Tesla's statewide TX fleet (Austin+Dallas+Houston combined) at 42 vehicles as of 2026-05-28, versus Waymo's 577 (TechCrunch 2026-05-28); that statewide TX count reportedly grew to ~175 by 2026-07-03 (Benzinga). Independent tracker reports put Dallas-specific unsupervised count at ~5 (2026-05-13, CleanTechnica) then ~3 (2026-05-26, Electrek).

access_type_at_launch: Public Robotaxi app (Android/iOS); fully unsupervised from day one, no safety driver or in-car monitor
current_status: Active; unsupervised; very small/newly launched fleet
official_fleet_size: unknown (Tesla did not disclose a fleet number at launch)
notes: Miami was included in the 7-city 1H-2026 expansion list announced 2026-01-28. Launched 2026-07-03 as Tesla's first driverless (no in-car safety monitor) market outside Texas/California (TechTimes 2026-07-04; Electrek 2026-07-03; Fox News). Geofence ~10-14 sq mi in western Miami-Dade, excluding downtown and Brickell (Fox News; TechTimes). Field reports / plate-spotting cited by Automotive World put the visible fleet at 2 vehicles on launch day, growing to 3 within 48 hours -- not an official Tesla figure.

access_type_at_launch: Not yet launched as of 2026-07-22 (staging/testing observed, no public rides confirmed)
current_status: Not launched; regulatory groundwork in place; Tesla's own Q1 2026 update reclassified Phoenix (with Miami/Orlando/Tampa/Las Vegas) from a firm ""1H 2026"" date to ""preparations underway"" (Electrek 2026-04-22)
notes: Arizona Department of Transportation granted Tesla a Transportation Network Company (TNC) permit effective 2025-11-17, allowing paid ride-hailing statewide but ONLY with a human safety driver -- it does not authorize driverless operation (InsideEVs; Electrek 2025-11-19; AZFamily 2025-11-19). ~60 Robotaxi-configured Model Ys (with rear-camera washers, a Robotaxi-specific hardware change) were spotted staged in a Phoenix parking lot in ~April 2026 (Basenor; Autonocion). Tesla has named 9 Arizona cities (incl. Phoenix, Scottsdale, Tempe) for eventual Cybercab rollout but has not confirmed an unsupervised/public launch date as of 2026-07-22.

access_type_at_launch: Not yet launched as of 2026-07-22 (permit application pending; testing/staging fleet spotted)
current_status: Not launched; AV testing permitted; commercial AVNC permit application still under regulatory review
notes: Nevada DOT approved Tesla for AV testing in the Las Vegas Valley (~Sept 2025). Tesla Robotaxi LLC filed an Autonomous Vehicle Network Company (AVNC) permit application with the Nevada Transportation Authority (Docket 26-05015) on 2026-06-05, requesting authority for up to 5,000 vehicles in year one; public comment period ran through 2026-07-05 and the application was still in staff review as of 2026-07-22, with no approval yet announced (DriveTeslaCanada; Review-Journal; CDC Gaming; Basenor). Tesla has invested ~$3.1M in a Las Vegas depot at 6170 Mohawk St with 8 Superchargers and 6 car lifts, and holds 2 Clark County business licenses (auto wash/detailing; Fremont St admin office) (Review-Journal). Gold-colored Cybercabs have been spotted testing in Southern Nevada (TeslaNorth 2026-06-22).
